research_question: Why can music trigger chills or goosebumps, and what evidence connects the response to prediction, reward, memory, and emotion?

sources.title: Music and the brain
notes: Music listening recruits distributed brain systems involved in attention, emotion, and memory.
No single brain area alone explains every music response.

sources.title: Music and the Brain
sources.publisher: McGill University, Office for Science and Society
notes: Research connects pleasurable music with reward-related systems.
Dopamine is one element of a broader set of interacting processes.

sources.title: Why Does Music Give Us Chills?
notes: Music chills can be triggered by musical build, surprise, and emotional context.
Listeners differ in their responses and reported triggers.

sources.title: Music-evoked chills and emotion
notes: Research examines individual differences in music-evoked chills and emotion.
Laboratory methods and subjective reports each have limitations.

sources.title: Music and emotion
sources.publisher: PubMed Central, National Institutes of Health
notes: Studies examine music, emotion, reward, and physiological responses.
Associations in brain studies do not establish one cause for every listener.
